note: Authoritative typed tool catalog dumped from gateway/src/tools.rs (the security boundary). Generated by `cargo test emit_catalog_json`; do not hand-edit.

tools.description: Report the current Houdini scene: hip file, frame, version, and /obj contents. The read-current-state tool: what's in the scene, what nodes exist, what have I built so far, current scene state, what does /obj look like right now. For the STRUCTURE of a network (node types + input wiring + flags) use read_network.
tools.name: scene_info

tools.description: Read a network's STRUCTURE as text — the durable, token-cheap map for rebuilding your picture of a big node graph (especially after a context compaction) WITHOUT spending budget on a screenshot. For the network at `path` (default /obj) returns each child node's name, type, INPUT WIRING (which sibling feeds each input slot, so the whole DAG is reconstructable), display/render/bypass/template flags, and child-count (is it a divable subnet). READ-ONLY, NO COOK — pure topology. Point it at /obj for the objects, or /obj/<geo> to read the SOP chain wire-by-wire. recursive=true descends into child subnets (depth-capped). params=true ALSO dumps each node's NON-DEFAULT parameters (the artist's actual choices — kept compact), their EXPRESSIONS / channel references verbatim, and the node comment — the fast way to reverse-engineer what an existing/in-progress network actually DOES, not just how it's wired (long/code values truncated, per-node count capped). Complements capture_ui panel=network (the visual) with the structural readout; use find_error_nodes for cook-error state, read_geo_stats for a node's geometry.
tools.name: read_network

params.desc: Network to read (default /obj). e.g. /obj to list objects, or /obj/mygeo to read its SOP chain.
params.name: path

params.desc: Also descend into child subnets, depth-capped by max_depth (default false = the immediate children of `path`).
params.name: recursive

params.desc: Also include each node's NON-DEFAULT parameters + expressions/channel refs + comment (default false = topology only). The reverse-engineering switch.
params.name: params

params.desc: Cap on total nodes returned (default 300); `truncated` flags when hit.
params.name: max_nodes

tools.description: Set the current timeline frame / playhead — jump to a point in time so subsequent cooks, snapshots, exports, or simulation reads evaluate at that frame. Moves the current time / animation frame; returns the resulting frame. Use before capturing a viewport or reading time-dependent geometry.
tools.name: set_frame

params.desc: Frame number to jump to (the timeline playhead / current time).
params.name: frame

tools.description: Set the display and/or render flag on a SOP or OBJ node — clean control over what's shown/rendered. Setting a SOP's display flag auto-clears sibling display flags in that network.
tools.name: set_display

params.desc: Set the display flag to this value (default true).
params.name: display

params.desc: If provided, set the render flag to this value; omitted leaves it unchanged.
params.name: render

tools.description: Delete a node (SOP or OBJ) from the scene. With reconnect=true the node's first input is bridged to each of its downstream output connections before deleting, so a mid-chain delete does not break the network (Houdini does not auto-bridge on delete); with no input, downstream inputs are just disconnected.
tools.name: delete_node

params.desc: Bridge the node's first input to its output connections before deleting so the downstream chain stays connected (default false).
params.name: reconnect

tools.description: Start fresh in the /obj network without a destructive File->New. mode='hide' (DEFAULT, non-destructive + reversible) turns the display flag OFF on every /obj object so the viewport clears but the nodes remain; mode='delete' REMOVES the /obj objects (destructive — like deleting each). `keep` is a comma-separated list of object names to leave untouched (e.g. the one thing you're keeping). Only touches /obj — never clears the hip file itself, never reaches unsaved work elsewhere. Returns {mode, affected, kept, remaining}. Prefer hide first (you can re-enable display); use delete only when you truly want the objects gone.
tools.name: clear_scene

params.desc: 'hide' (default, non-destructive: display off) or 'delete' (remove the /obj objects).
params.name: mode

params.desc: Comma-separated /obj object names to leave untouched.
params.name: keep

tools.description: Save / write the whole Houdini scene (all nodes and networks) to a .hip / .hipnc / .hiplc project file on disk, confined to the working directory — the 'save my work' / snapshot-the-session op. Preserves the full node graph so the scene can be reopened later. The path must end in .hip / .hipnc / .hiplc; the parent directory is created if needed.
tools.name: save_scene

params.desc: Output .hip / .hipnc / .hiplc scene-file path (confined to the working directory).
params.name: path

tools.description: Select a node (clearing any prior selection) and make it the current node. With dive=true, and if a Network Editor pane is open, set that pane's pwd to the node so its internal child graph is shown (a no-op when the node has no browsable interior).
tools.name: select_node

params.desc: Dive the Network Editor into this node so its child graph is shown (default false).
params.name: dive

tools.description: Frame the Scene Viewer on a node — the Shift+H 'home selected' equivalent, for precise framing in mixed-scale scenes where frame-all is useless. With node, select it first then frame it; without, frame the current selection.
tools.name: frame_selected

params.desc: Node path to select and frame; omit to frame the current selection.
params.name: node

tools.description: Auto-arrange a network's children so freshly added nodes don't stack — the Shift+L equivalent. Reach for this when the graph is a stacked mess, nodes are overlapping / piled on top of each other, or you just want to clean up / organize / tidy / untangle the node layout. parent is the network whose children to lay out (e.g. /obj or /obj/terrain).
tools.name: layout_nodes

params.desc: Network node path whose children to lay out.
params.name: parent

tools.description: Read-only diagnostic: scan a subtree for nodes in an error (and optionally warning) state and report their paths, types, and messages so an AI agent can self-correct. root (default /obj) scopes the scan (root plus every descendant); a guarded cook is attempted per node so a broken node (e.g. a File SOP pointing at a missing path) surfaces as a captured error, not a raised exception. Pure introspection — no node is created, deleted, or mutated. Reach for this when you're stuck: my node errored, something broke, why isn't this working, nothing's showing up, the build failed, the graph is red — diagnose, troubleshoot, debug the graph, find the cook error, figure out what went wrong.
tools.name: find_error_nodes

params.desc: Also report nodes that only have warnings.
params.name: include_warnings

tools.description: Run up to 64 tool ops in ONE call to cut per-call latency (e.g. build a node chain in a single round-trip). Each op is `{name, arguments}` and is dispatched through the EXACT same path as a direct call: schema-validated, numerics clamped, filesystem paths confined to the working directory, and audited in order. This is a convenience envelope, NOT a privilege escalation — a batch can only invoke real catalog tools (no arbitrary code, no non-catalog names) and cannot nest (an op named 'batch' is rejected). Ops run in order and continue on error unless stop_on_error=true, in which case the batch stops at the first failing op. Returns a per-op result list ({name, ok, result|error}); isError is true if any op errored.
tools.name: batch

params.desc: Ordered list (1..64) of ops to run, each `{"name": "<tool>", "arguments": { ... }}`. arguments is optional (defaults to {}). Every op is validated and confined exactly as a direct call; 'batch' is not a valid op name.
params.name: ops

params.desc: If true, stop at the first op that errors and return what ran so far (default false = continue on error).
params.name: stop_on_error

tools.description: Start here — getting started, how to use this server, an overview of what it can do, orientation and first steps for a new agent. A cheap, offline orientation call: returns what this Houdini MCP server can do (its typed tool count broken down by category) plus pointers to the deeper references you can query while planning — node_reference (real node types + real parameter names), vex_reference (VEX builtins + a wrangle workflow guide; reference-only, never executes VEX), recipe_reference (canonical tool-mapped workflow recipes), and the running Houdini's local HTTP help server. Call it first when planning a task so you discover exactly which node chains and VEX are possible before building. Takes no arguments; runs offline (no Houdini session).
tools.name: capabilities

tools.description: Query the authoritative live-probed Houdini 21.0.671 node reference — verified node types and their real parameter names, the source of truth for what node chains are possible. Pass node=<type> for its parameters, search=<substring> to find node types, or category=<Sop|Object|Dop|Driver|Cop|Cop2|Lop|Vop|Chop|Shop|Top> to list one (Cop = the 262 Copernicus 2D-image node types); no args returns a summary. Sibling references: vex_reference (VEX builtins), recipe_reference (tool-mapped workflows), and the running Houdini's local HTTP help server (URL from capabilities). Runs offline (no Houdini session needed) — use it while planning.
tools.name: node_reference

params.desc: Exact node type name -> its probed parameters (e.g. heightfield_erode::3.0).
params.name: node

params.desc: Substring to find matching node type names across categories.
params.name: search

params.desc: List node types in one category.
params.name: category

tools.description: Query the authoritative offline Houdini 21.0.671 VEX reference: 1073 builtin functions (verbatim signatures, summaries, help groups) plus a curated wrangle workflow/patterns guide. REFERENCE ONLY — this serves documentation, it never runs VEX. The executor is deliberately data-only (there is no wrangle/exec path, which would be RCE); use this to propose correct VEX *text* for the USER to paste into a wrangle node by hand (the wrangle handoff). When a task needs logic typed tools can't express (threshold breaking, cluster boundary, custom masks — recipe steps flag these as `wrangle_opportunity`), PROACTIVELY surface a wrangle: topic=surface explains WHEN to offer + the consent handshake (propose + teach; run only with user consent via set_attrib_expr+allow_attrib_expr, or hand it over to paste). Pass function=<name> for its signature(s)+summary(+guide examples), search=<substring> to find functions by name or summary, category=<group> to list one group, or topic=<key> for a guide section; no args returns a summary plus the reference-only boundary note. Sibling references: node_reference (node types + parameters), recipe_reference (tool-mapped workflows), and the running Houdini's local HTTP help server (URL from capabilities). Runs offline (no Houdini session) — use it while planning.
tools.name: vex_reference

params.desc: Exact VEX function name -> its signature(s), summary, categories, and any matching guide examples (e.g. fit, pcopen, curlnoise).
params.name: function

params.desc: Substring to match across function names and summaries.
params.name: search

params.desc: List all functions in one help group.
params.name: category

params.desc: Return a section of the curated VEX workflow guide. Fundamentals: handoff, surface, contexts, types, core, noise, lookups, groups, patterns, gotchas, index. Cookbook domains: kinefx/curves/matrix (rig, curve & matrix math); rbd/pyro/flip/pops/vellum/crowds (sim & secondary sim); orient/noise2/pointclouds (instancing & procedural distribution); modeling/uv/heightfield (geometry, UV & terrain); attribs/groups_adv/vdb (attribute, group & volume recipes); sceneprep/solver (utility/debug & solver-time feedback).
params.name: topic

tools.description: Canonical, tool-mapped workflow recipes — how to ACTUALLY do X with this server's tools, and the ROUTER that picks which recipe fits what you're looking at. New here? Call `capabilities` first for the data-only boundary, the build-to-a-budget governor, and the conventions these recipes assume (plant OUT_ nulls, verify each step, hand off at WIRE-ONLY / wrangle gates). Each recipe is an ordered sequence of real tools + the params that matter + per-step landmark (the OUT_* null to plant) / verify (the cheap read_geo_stats or milestone snapshot check to run) / geometry_out (the class it emits). THE FRONT DOOR: classify=<what you're looking at> ('a building', 'a facade photo', 'terrain', 'water') -> the routing table's matching lane + entry_recipe; then recipe=<entry_recipe> for the ordered steps. Also: recipe=<id> -> full steps; domain=<name> -> a domain's recipes; search=<substring> (indexes step tools too, so you can find a recipe by the tool it uses); no args -> the recipe index + routing table. Read-only + offline; serves data, never actuates. Sibling references: node_reference, vex_reference, and the running Houdini's local HTTP help server (URL from capabilities).
tools.name: recipe_reference

params.desc: What you're looking at / want to build (e.g. 'a building', 'a facade photo', 'terrain', 'water splash') -> the routing table rows (lane + entry_recipe). Empty string returns the whole routing table. START HERE.
params.name: classify

params.desc: Exact recipe id -> its full ordered steps + per-step landmark/verify/geometry_out + key params + tips (e.g. flip_splash, image_to_3d_spine, model_hardsurface_kit).
params.name: recipe

params.desc: List the recipes in one domain (brief). Domains: flip, pyro, rbd, procedural, material, terrain, vellum, modeling, ocean, capture (see the index's `domains`).
params.name: domain

params.desc: Substring to match across recipe id/title/summary/classify + the step tool names + tool_manifest. Also indexes gated-capability opportunity signals — search 'render'/'solver'/'vop'/'wrangle'/'opportunity' to surface recipe steps that carry a *_opportunity handoff (where the AI should proactively offer a WIRE-ONLY render/ROP, a deferred solver, a VOP graph, or a consented safe-VEX wrangle).
params.name: search

params.name: source

params.desc: flat = local heightfields; globe = ECEF globe tiles.

Emits: a heightfield/volume (native voxel space); needs a heightfield input.

params.desc: SOP node path of the source height volume.

params.desc: Extra padding voxels around the window.

tools.description: Transfer/blend features from a patch height volume (input1) onto a base (input0) with a smooth boundary — mosaic adjacent DEM tiles or stamp a masked region. scale uniformly scales the patch (grid + feature magnitude) before transfer; heightscale scales only the transferred feature heights; tx/tz translate and ry rotates-about-Y the patch before transfer; centerpatch pivots those handles on the masked region. Emits: a heightfield/volume (native voxel space); needs a base heightfield (input0) + a patch heightfield (input1).
tools.name: heightfield_patch

params.desc: SOP node path of the base height volume.
params.name: input

params.desc: SOP node path of the patch height volume (input1).
params.name: patch

params.desc: Uniform patch scale (grid + feature magnitude, default 1).
params.name: scale

params.desc: Scale of the transferred feature heights only (default 1).
params.name: heightscale

params.desc: Center the patch on its mask so tx/tz/ry pivot there (default on).
params.name: centerpatch

tools.description: Convert a height volume into renderable/exportable geometry. conversion picks the output (poly | polysoup dense-non-editable | vdb 3D volume); surftype is the polygon connectivity (triangles/quads are the useful terrain layouts); lod is Density = output-resolution ratio (0.5 = half res, 2 = 4x supersample); bake_colors bakes the heightfield material onto the mesh as point Cd so the deliverable carries the gradient; extrude_base + depth add a solid extruded base (watertight for print/CFD). Emits: POLYGONS (or polysoup/VDB per `conversion`) from a heightfield VOLUME; needs a heightfield input.
tools.name: convert_heightfield

params.desc: SOP node path of the source height volume.
params.name: input

params.desc: Density: output-resolution ratio (1.0 = full res, <1 = decimate, >1 = supersample).
params.name: lod

params.desc: Bake the heightfield's color onto the output mesh as point Cd (default on).
params.name: bake_colors

params.desc: Add an extruded solid base under the surface.
params.name: extrude_base

params.desc: Flatten the extruded base (default on; off = draped base).
params.name: flatten_base

tools.description: Even-triangulation remesh (Remesh 2.0) — rebuild a triangulated / scan surface into well-shaped, evenly sized triangles for smoothing, simulation, or clean deformation. targetsize is the target edge length in world units (smaller = denser mesh, higher polycount); sizing=uniform gives one size everywhere, sizing=adaptive concentrates smaller triangles on curvature (density = adaptive target-density multiplier). gradation biases the uniform<->adaptive blend (0 uniform .. 1 fully curvature-adaptive). iterations = smoothing/optimization passes; smoothing = per-pass point-relaxation strength. min_edge/max_edge clamp the produced edge length. Preserve detail with hard_edges/hard_points (feature groups held rigid) and harden_uv_seams (+uv_attrib). Input: one triangulated surface; quads are triangulated first. Cost scales as ~1/targetsize^2 — keep targetsize sane on big scans. Emits: an evenly-triangulated POLYGON surface; needs a polygonal/manifold surface (analytic primitives or open curves misbehave — divide/convert first).
tools.name: remesh

params.desc: Target triangle edge length in world units (default 0.2). Smaller = denser mesh.
params.name: targetsize

params.desc: uniform = one edge length everywhere; adaptive = smaller triangles on curvature (default uniform).
params.name: sizing

params.desc: Lower clamp on produced edge length (enables useminsize).
params.name: min_edge

params.desc: Upper clamp on produced edge length (enables usemaxsize).
params.name: max_edge

params.desc: Adaptivity: 0 = uniform, higher = adapt edge length to curvature (default 0.25).
params.name: gradation

params.desc: Edge group to preserve as hard features (not smoothed away).
params.name: hard_edges

params.desc: Point group to preserve as hard features.
params.name: hard_points

params.desc: Preserve UV seams as hard edges.
params.name: harden_uv_seams

tools.description: Decimate (PolyReduce 2.0) — collapse a mesh to a fraction of its polycount for LOD / real-time delivery while keeping silhouette and features. target chooses what the reduction targets: poly_percent / pt_percent (percentage, the default, via percentage) or poly_count / pt_count (an absolute finalcount — the LOD workhorse). qualitytolerance trades quality for speed. Protect detail with hard_edges/hard_points (held rigid), boundary_weight (mesh-border retention), seam_weight (UV/attribute seams), preserve_quads (avoid triangulating quads), and retain_attrib (a float point attribute biasing where triangles are kept). Input: one polygon mesh. Reduction is lossy — chain heightfield/scan cleanup first, then reduce last. Emits: a decimated POLYGON mesh; needs a polygon mesh input.
tools.name: polyreduce

params.desc: What the reduction targets: percentage of polys/points (default poly_percent, uses percentage) or an absolute poly/point count (uses finalcount).
params.name: target

params.desc: Reduction quality tolerance (higher = faster, lower quality; default ~0).
params.name: qualitytolerance

params.desc: Keep quad topology where possible instead of collapsing to tris.
params.name: preserve_quads

params.desc: Edge group to hold as hard features during decimation (protect scan borders / creases).
params.name: hard_edges

params.desc: Point group to hold as hard features.
params.name: hard_points

params.desc: A float point attribute (e.g. 'retention') that biases where detail is kept.
params.name: retain_attrib

tools.description: Turn a point cloud into a mesh (cloud → VDB → polygons) with optional reduction, color transfer, and export. Emits: a POLYGON mesh in a fresh /obj geo; needs a point-cloud input.
tools.name: mesh_pointcloud

params.desc: SOP node path of the source point cloud.

tools.description: One-shot scatter-and-instance: randomly scatter `count` points across a target surface and copy/instance a source shape onto every point (foliage, rocks, ice chunks, debris, greebles). Creates a new /obj geometry containing surface -> scatter -> copytopoints. target = an existing surface SOP path to scatter on (defaults to a 100x100 grid). source = a primitive keyword (box/sphere/tube/torus/grid/circle) or an existing node path to copy. density_attrib biases placement by a point float attribute (e.g. a heightfield mask / slope) so instances grow only where allowed. seed reshuffles the scatter. COST: count multiplies the source's polycount — keep count modest for heavy sources. For copying onto EXISTING points use copy_to_points; to only scatter points use scatter. Emits: copied/instanced geometry (a fresh /obj geo of surface→scatter→copytopoints); needs a scatter target surface + a source shape.
tools.name: scatter_copy

params.desc: Number of scatter points (each gets a copy of the source — cost multiplier).
params.name: count

params.desc: SOP path of the surface to scatter on (defaults to a grid).
params.name: target

params.desc: Primitive keyword (box/sphere/tube/torus/grid/circle) or SOP path to copy onto points.
params.name: source

params.desc: Uniform scale of each copied source shape.
params.name: scale

params.desc: Name of a point float attribute on the target that biases where points land (e.g. a heightfield mask / slope / occlusion) — mask-driven placement.
params.name: density_attrib

tools.description: Create a camera to MATCH A REFERENCE PHOTO / recreate an image / camera-solve a shot — set the intrinsics so a render lines up with a target picture. focal length (mm) + aperture (mm) = field of view / perspective compression (shorter focal or wider aperture = wider FOV); resx/resy = resolution gate; aspect. Depth of field: focus distance + fstop (smaller = shallower/blurrier bokeh). near/far clipping. projection: perspective (default) | orthographic | sphere (360 latlong/equirectangular VR/dome) | cylinder; orthographic uses orthowidth. Lens/tilt-shift via win/winsize. **background = a REFERENCE PLATE / backdrop image (read-confined) so snapshot composites your geometry OVER the target for registered verification.** Position with t=[x,y,z] + r=[x,y,z]; camera_aim points it at a target; snapshot renders through it.
tools.name: add_camera

params.desc: Aperture / horizontal film-back (mm) — wider = wider FOV.
params.name: aperture

params.desc: Projection: perspective | orthographic | sphere (360 equirectangular/latlong panoramic) | cylinder (cylindrical panorama).

tools.description: Screenshot / see / read the LIVE Houdini interface, ISOLATED to a single pane on request. LEAK-SAFE by construction: captures Houdini's OWN rendered content only — NEVER a screen grab — so another window sitting in front of Houdini (the normal case while an agent drives) can't bleed into the image. panel='viewport' renders Houdini's own GL 3D viewport (occlusion-immune, the real scene) — frame it first (frame_selected / home_view) or pass frame_view=true; panel='network'/'parameters'/'spreadsheet'/'window' grab the Houdini window's own painted UI (the 3D-viewport region is blank in THESE — use panel='viewport' for the 3D). Inlined so the agent SEES it. This is the CHEAP, inline inspection path — prefer it for iterative build-then-look verification; snapshot fires a heavier OpenGL ROP / flipbook export, so reserve that for a final beauty/verify render. Unlike snapshot (a clean GL render), this reads the real interface (node wires, parameter fields, attribute values). AUTO-FITS the ~1 MB inline cap: resx/resy/max_dimension downscale + auto PNG→JPEG shrink, so a smaller image is returned instead of an error. Returns {path, panel, requested, width, height, res, format, bytes, downscaled}; `panel` echoes what was ACTUALLY captured (reads 'window' if the requested pane was not open).
tools.name: capture_ui

A pane not currently open falls back to the whole window (reported back in `panel`).
params.name: panel

params.desc: Only for panel='viewport': frame-all the scene in the GL grab before capturing (like snapshot's frame_view). Otherwise the viewport is captured as it is currently framed — call frame_selected / home_view first to aim it.
params.name: frame_view

params.desc: Max capture width in pixels — the grab is downscaled to fit within it (aspect preserved; never upscaled).
params.name: resx

params.desc: Max capture height in pixels — the grab is downscaled to fit within it (aspect preserved; never upscaled).

tools.description: See/screenshot the 3D result — a single OpenGL PNG of the viewport/camera returned INLINE in the tool result (the agent's eyes for image->3D verification). `camera` = the reliable offscreen OpenGL-ROP path (honours resx/resy + aa); no camera = viewport flipbook (needs an open Scene Viewer). PNG is confined to the working directory; the return echoes the ACTUAL output `res` [w,h] + `confined_to_working_dir`. Pair with read_geo_stats to catch scale errors a picture hides. COST: each call fires an OpenGL ROP / viewport flipbook export — for quick iterative viewport checks prefer capture_ui panel=viewport (cheap, inline) and reserve snapshot for a final beauty/verify render. For the LIVE UI (network editor / parameters / arranged graph) use capture_ui instead. HEAVY-SCENE GUARD: never on a heavy heightfield/volume scene — the GL grab can freeze the session.

tools.description: Hydraulic + thermal erosion at a chosen feature scale (HeightField Erode 3.0). params.desc: Name for the new /obj geometry (must not exist).
params.name: name

params.desc: For sphere/tube/circle: emit real polygons (default true) so downstream boolean/remesh/scatter works; false = raw analytic primitive.
params.name: as_polygons

tools.description: Loft/skin a surface across ordered profile curves — input is a SOP holding several profile primitives (merge parallel curves first); skin lofts across them in prim order. output_polygons=false yields a spline mesh; v_wrap=wv closes the loft into a loop. Polycount ≈ (num_profiles-1) × points_per_profile — governor-advised. Emits: polygons (or a spline mesh when output_polygons=false); needs several profile CURVES merged into one input, not an analytic primitive.
tools.name: skin

params.desc: SOP holding the merged profile curves.
params.name: input

params.desc: Close the loft in V (wv = loop last→first profile).
params.name: v_wrap

params.desc: Keep the source profile prims in the output.
params.name: keep_primitives

tools.description: Lathe a profile curve around an axis → a surface of revolution (vase, tube, bottle, wheel, lampshade). axis+origin define the spin axis (default Y through origin); divisions = sides; revolve_type=openarc|closedarc + angle=[start,end] make a partial arc; caps closes the ends. Polycount ≈ (profile_points-1) × divisions — governor-advised. Emits: a polygon/mesh surface of revolution; needs a profile CURVE input (points offset from the axis), not an analytic primitive.
tools.name: revolve

params.desc: Profile curve SOP (points offset from the axis).
params.name: input

params.desc: Sides around the axis (polycount ≈ profile points × divisions; node default 12, soft-max 50).
params.name: divisions

params.desc: Restrict to a profile prim group.
params.name: group

tools.description: Reflect geometry across a plane and (by default) weld the seam. axis=x|y|z is a shortcut for the plane normal (or give dirx/diry/dirz + originx/originy/originz); dist offsets the plane. keep_original=false replaces with only the mirror; weld fuses the seam; operation=clip cuts at the plane instead of reflecting. Emits: the input geometry class, reflected (polygons in → polygons out); needs real point/poly geometry to weld the seam.
tools.name: mirror

params.desc: Plane normal x (if not using axis).
params.name: dirx

params.desc: Offset the plane along its normal.
params.name: dist

params.desc: Reverse normals on the mirrored copy.
params.name: flip_normals

tools.description: Dissolve an edge (or point) group, MERGING the adjacent faces — topology simplification (unlike blast, which deletes and leaves a hole). The component kind is inferred from the group. invert=keep dissolves everything except the group; remove_inline_points cleans redundant colinear points. Emits: polygons with the group's faces MERGED (topology simplified); needs an edge/point group on a POLYGON mesh (build it with the group tools first).

params.desc: Edge (or point) group to dissolve (built via the group tools).

tools.description: Bridge two edge loops into a connecting tube/skirt (polybridge). BOTH loops must live on ONE input as two edge groups (src_group / dst_group, built via the group tools and merged into one stream) — this is NOT two-input. divisions subdivides the skirt; twists/pairing_shift/reverse_src/reverse_dst fix twisting or inside-out pairing; thickness shells it. Emits: polygons (the connecting skirt/tube); needs ONE polygon input carrying both edge-loop groups.
tools.name: bridge

params.desc: SOP holding both edge loops (merged into one stream).
params.name: input

params.desc: Rotate vertex pairing between loops (fix twist).

tools.description: Wrap-deform input by the motion of a cage: rest_cage (input1) → deformed_cage (input2). The dense mesh follows the low-res cage delta — reuse a coarse edit on dense scan geometry. radius (capture radius) must roughly match the cage point spacing, or little/nothing binds. Emits: the input geometry class, wrap-deformed; needs THREE inputs — geometry (0), rest cage (1), deformed cage (2).

tools.description: Write creaseweight on an edge group so a downstream subdivide keeps those edges SHARP — the key to credible subdivision-surface hard-surface modeling. group = edge group, weight = crease value (0..10), op = addto|set|delete. A bare call triangulates. Emits: polygons (triangulated/subdivided/bricked); needs polygonal input (analytic primitives have no faces to divide).

params.desc: Smooth subdivision iterations — each level ~4x polycount (node soft-max 5).

tools.description: Copy/instance the source SOP geometry onto every point of the target SOP (Copy to Points 2.0) — the core instancing op for foliage, rocks, debris, greebles, crowds. Each copy is transformed by the target point's TRANSFORM intrinsics: N/up orient the copy, pscale scales it, orient (quaternion) rotates it, v/pivot also apply — author those on the target points first (e.g. via attribute_randomize) to vary the copies. Non-transform attributes named in target_attribs (default Cd) are also carried from the target POINTS onto the copies for per-instance colour/variation (a target point attribute of that name must exist). source = geometry to copy (input0, auto-bridged across networks); target = points that receive copies (input1). pack = output lightweight packed primitives (far cheaper memory for large counts). id_attrib matches a variant/piece attribute on BOTH sides for multi-asset instancing. target_group/source_group restrict to a named group. COST: output prims = source prims x target points. To also scatter the points in one call use scatter_copy. Emits: copied geometry, or PACKED prims when pack=true; needs a source geo (input0) + a target POINT cloud (input1). (This is the SOP geometry copy/instancing — NOT a cop_* 2D-image copy.)

A cross-network source is auto-bridged.

tools.description: Author/modify a float attribute with a value pattern (attribadjustfloat). `input` is input 0. attrib/attrib_class target the attribute; operation how the value is applied; value_type the pattern source; single_value the constant; min_value/max_value the random range; seed the seed; blend fades the effect. Data-only (the node's VEXpression + color-map file paths are not exposed).
tools.name: attrib_adjust_float

params.desc: How the value is applied (default add).
params.name: operation

params.desc: Clamp result to a minimum (default off).
params.name: clamp_min

params.desc: Clamp result to a maximum (default off).
params.name: clamp_max

tools.description: Author/modify an integer attribute with a value pattern (attribadjustinteger). `input` is input 0. attrib/attrib_class target the attribute; operation how applied; value_type the pattern; single_value the constant; min_value/max_value the random integer range; step_size an optional quantisation; seed the seed. Data-only (VEXpression + color-map file paths not exposed).
tools.name: attrib_adjust_integer

params.desc: How the value is applied (default add).
params.name: operation

tools.description: Author/modify a vector attribute's direction and/or length (attribadjustvector). `input` is input 0. attrib/attrib_class target the attribute; adjust_quantity picks direction+length / direction-only / length-only; dirlen_operation how applied; value the constant vector [x,y,z]; reverse flips; pre_normalize/post_normalize make unit length; seed the seed. Data-only (VEXpression not exposed).
tools.name: attrib_adjust_vector

params.desc: How the value is applied (default add).
params.name: dirlen_operation

params.desc: Make vectors unit length before adjust (default off).
params.name: pre_normalize

params.desc: Make vectors unit length after adjust (default off).
params.name: post_normalize

tools.description: Author/modify a color (Cd) attribute (attribadjustcolor). `input` is input 0. attrib/attrib_class target the attribute; blend_space RGB or HSV; operation the blend op; value_type the pattern; color the constant color [r,g,b]; seed the seed. Data-only (VEXpression + color-map file paths not exposed).
tools.name: attrib_adjust_color

tools.description: Identity/ordering controls for an array attribute (attribadjustarray). `input` is input 0. attrib/attrib_class target the array attribute; array_type its element type; sort/reverse reorder each array. (Per-entry add/remove/replace edits live in a multiparm block and are not exposed in this flat wrap.)
tools.name: attrib_adjust_array

tools.description: High-level controls for a dictionary attribute (attribadjustdict). `input` is input 0. attrib/attrib_class target the dict attribute; remove_keys + keys strip keys by pattern; delete_empty drops the attribute when a dict becomes empty. (Per-key rename/set edits live in multiparm blocks and are not exposed in this flat wrap.)
tools.name: attrib_adjust_dict

params.desc: Delete the attribute if a dict becomes empty (default on).
params.name: delete_empty

tools.description: Combine attributes into a destination via a math op (attribcombine). `input` is input 0; an optional `source` geometry can be wired to input 1 and referenced with src_input='second'. dst_attrib is the destination; src_attrib the first source; operation the math; overall_scale post-scales; attrib_class the element class. create_missing makes the destination if absent.
tools.name: attrib_combine

params.desc: Read the source from the first or second input (default first).
params.name: src_input

params.desc: Create the destination if missing (default on).
params.name: create_missing

params.desc: Delete source attributes after combine (default off).
params.name: delete_source

params.desc: Error if an attribute is missing (default on).
params.name: error_on_missing

tools.description: Fill/propagate an attribute across a surface by solving a field (attribfill). `input` is input 0. mode picks the solve (arrival-time eikonal / interpolate poisson / blur heat / extrapolate transport). attrib is the attribute to fill; source the 'attribute to match' selecting seeds; weights/speed optional control attributes; boundary an optional boundary group; diffusion_time the blur time step.
tools.name: attrib_fill

tools.description: Author a per-point fade weight ramping in/holding/out over frames (attribfade), typically to fade particles/pieces in and out. `input` is input 0. fade_attrib names the output float; fade_in/fade_hold/fade_out set the frame durations; frame_offset shifts the curve; start_attrib/duration_attrib optionally drive start-frame/hold per element.
tools.name: attrib_fade

tools.description: Remap a numeric attribute's values from an input range to an output range, optionally through a ramp (attribremap). `input` is input 0. in_name is the attribute to remap; out_name an optional new name (blank = in place); input_min/max the source range; output_min/max the target range; clamp_type how out-of-range values are handled; use_ramp toggles the remap ramp; attrib_class the element class.
tools.name: attrib_remap

params.desc: Optional new attribute name (blank = in place).
params.name: out_name

tools.description: Reorder points/vertices/prims by the value of an attribute (attribsort). `input` is input 0. attrib is the sort key; attrib_class the element class; component which vector component to sort on; order ascending or descending; use_indices/indices optionally write the argsort permutation to an attribute.
tools.name: attrib_sort

tools.description: For each element, find the element(s) in a SEARCH geometry with a matching attribute value (attribfind). `input` (query geometry) is input 0; `search` (the geometry to search in) MUST be wired to input 1 — the node errors without it. query_attrib is the value looked up; search_in_attrib the attribute searched; mode what to record; tolerance the match tolerance.
tools.name: attrib_find

params.desc: Geometry to search in (input 1) — required for the node to cook.
params.name: search

params.desc: Restrict the query to a group.
params.name: group

params.desc: Attribute searched in the search geometry (default uv).
params.name: search_in_attrib

params.desc: Treat the attribute as a wrapped texture UV (default on).
params.name: wrap_unit_cube

tools.description: Sample a source into a point attribute along UVs (attribfrommap). `input` is input 0. map_source picks the source: 'off' = a Cd color attribute on the geometry, 'on' = a texture file (map_file), 'vol' = a volume primitive (volume_name) from the input. export_attribute names the output; attrib_type float or vector; uv_attrib the UV set; color_channel which channel. map_file is a read-only, working-dir-confined asset path (only for the 'on' source).
tools.name: attrib_from_map

params.desc: Source: color attribute / file / volume (default on).
params.name: map_source

params.desc: UV attribute to sample along (default uv).
params.name: uv_attrib

tools.description: Import another node's PARAMETER VALUES onto geometry as attributes (attribfromparm). `input` is input 0. node_path is the source Houdini node whose parameters are read; method how they map; attrib the output attribute name; parm_filter/category_filter select which parameters; evaluate reads evaluated values. Data-only: reads parameter values, runs no code.
tools.name: attrib_from_parm

params.desc: Source node whose parameters are read.
params.name: node_path

tools.description: Assign a per-piece attribute value across named pieces (attribfrompieces). `input` (geometry with pieces) is input 0; a `pieces` geometry MUST be wired to input 1 — the node errors without a second source. piece_attrib names the piece id; attrib the attribute to write; attrib_type numeric or string; mode how values are distributed; seed/shuffle randomise. (The 'vex' mode + VEXpression inputs are not exposed.)
tools.name: attrib_from_pieces

params.desc: Pieces source geometry (input 1) — required for the node to cook.
params.name: pieces

tools.description: Copy/mirror an attribute from one side of geometry to the other (attribmirror). `input` is input 0. attrib picks WHAT to copy (color / texture-uv / other); attrib_name the specific name when 'other'; mirror_method plane/topology/mapping; origin+direction define the mirror plane; transform how mirrored vectors/uvs/points are reoriented; string_replace + search/replace remap side-tagged string values (e.g. L_* -> R_*).
tools.name: attrib_mirror

params.desc: Use the group as source or destination (default destination).
params.name: use_group_as

params.desc: How mirrored values are reoriented (default nomirror).
params.name: transform

tools.description: Set up a paintable attribute (attribpaint). `input` is input 0. attrib names the attribute; attrib_type color/float/integer; fg_color/fg_float/fg_int the foreground value; enable_mirror mirrors strokes. NOTE: the actual painting is an interactive viewport operation; headless this configures the node and passes geometry through (the stroke-data and cache FILE parms are not exposed).
tools.name: attrib_paint

params.desc: Mirror strokes across a plane (default off).
params.name: enable_mirror

tools.description: Find/replace on string attribute values (attribstringedit). `input` is input 0. Enable the classes to touch with points/prims/detail/vertex + the matching *_list of attribute names. A single find -> replace pair is applied to the enabled attributes. (Additional replacement pairs and regex mode live in a multiparm block and are not exposed here.)
tools.name: attrib_string_edit

tools.description: Build a smooth polygon patch surface across a hull/cage of curves or a mesh (polypatch) — tidy a rough curve cage into a clean subdiv-ready surface. basis = smoothing basis (cardinal | bspline); connectivity = how hull rows/cols connect into the patch; divisions [u,v] = output resolution; close_u/close_v wrap it; output_polygons emits polys instead of a mesh primitive. Emits: a mesh/polygon patch; needs a hull of curves or a mesh as input.
tools.name: poly_patch

params.desc: SOP node path — the hull curves / mesh to patch.
params.name: input

params.desc: Emit polygons instead of a mesh primitive.
params.name: output_polygons

tools.description: Skin a polygon surface across a sequence of cross-section curves (polyloft). `input` (input 0) carries the ordered cross-sections MERGED into one stream (e.g. merge two circles); optional `rest` (input 1) is rest geometry. connect_closest_ends auto-orders open curves; consolidate + dist weld near points; minimize picks the triangulation metric; close_u/close_v wrap; create_group + group_name tag the new polys. Emits: a lofted polygon surface; needs >=2 cross-section curves merged into input 0.
tools.name: poly_loft

params.desc: SOP node path — the ordered cross-sections merged into one stream (input 0).
params.name: input

params.desc: Auto-order open curves by closest ends.
params.name: connect_closest_ends

params.desc: Create a polygon group for the new polys.
params.name: create_group

params.desc: Name of the created polygon group.
params.name: group_name

tools.description: Fit a smooth spline through a polyline's points and re-output it as a resampled polygon curve (polyspline) — turn a coarse control polygon into a smooth curve. spline_type = interpolation basis; closure whether to close; division_method how sample density is distributed; segment_length / divisions / sample_divisions the output resolution; tension the CV tension. Emits: a polygon curve; needs a polyline / face input.
tools.name: poly_spline

params.desc: SOP node path — the polyline / face to smooth.
params.name: input

tools.description: Fit circular-arc / ellipse / helix splines through a control polygon (circlespline) — perfectly round curvature a freeform spline can't give. spline_type (hybrid | circle | ellipse | helix); helix_type the winding style; reparm_strength re-parametrizes for even spacing; segment_divisions the output resolution; output_tangent + tangent_attrib write a tangent attribute. Emits: a curve; needs a control polygon input.
tools.name: circle_spline

params.desc: SOP node path — the control polygon.
params.name: input

tools.description: Fill open polygon boundaries (unshared edges) with cap polygons (polycap) — seal a tube/extrusion end or a hole ring. Without a `group`, cap_all seals EVERY unshared-edge loop; reverse flips cap orientation; triangulate fans the cap into triangles; unique un-shares cap points; update_normals recomputes point normals. Emits: the input plus cap polygons; needs polygonal input with open boundaries.
tools.name: poly_cap

params.desc: Cap ALL unshared-edge loops when no group.
params.name: cap_all

tools.description: Add end/pole caps to NURBS/mesh surfaces and open curves, per U/V boundary (cap) — close the ends of tubes/spheres/revolved surfaces. first_u_cap / last_u_cap / first_v_cap / last_v_cap each pick a style (none | facet | share | round | tangent); divisions_u / divisions_v the rounded-cap resolution; scale_u / scale_v bulge the caps. Emits: the input plus caps; needs a surface with U/V boundaries.
tools.name: cap

tools.description: Build a smooth transition surface between adjacent primitives / two curves (fillet) — round hard junctions between surfaces. `input` = the primitives to fillet (input 0); optional `aux` = auxiliary source (input 1). fillet: which prims (all | group | skip); inc how many prims each fillet spans; loop wraps last to first; direction (ujoin | vjoin); fillet_type the transition shape (freeform | convex | circular); order the surface order; cut trims the originals; seamless matches the input. Emits: fillet surfaces; needs >=2 adjacent primitives in input 0.
tools.name: fillet

params.desc: SOP node path — the primitives to fillet (input 0).
params.name: input

tools.description: Blend/stitch two adjacent surface HULLS together along shared boundaries (stitch). `input` = the surface hulls to stitch (input 0, e.g. two merged NURBS/mesh grids); optional `aux` = auxiliary hull (input 1). stitch: which prims (all | group | skip); inc the span; loop wraps; direction (ujoin | vjoin); tolerance / bias the blend; do_stitch / tangent / sharp the continuity. Emits: stitched surfaces; input MUST be surface hulls (open polylines error 'must be a hull').
tools.name: stitch

params.desc: SOP node path — the surface hulls to stitch (input 0).
params.name: input

tools.description: Connect a sequence of separate primitives (curves or surfaces) end-to-end into a single continuous primitive (join) — turn many little pieces into one long primitive. `input` = the prims to join, merged into one stream. join_op: which prims (all | group | skip); inc the span; direction (ujoin | vjoin); blend + tolerance + bias the seam; loop wraps last to first; only_connected joins only topological neighbours. Emits: joined primitives; needs >=2 primitives in input 0.
tools.name: join

params.desc: SOP node path — the primitives to join (merged into one stream).
params.name: input

tools.description: Fold/rotate polygons about a hinge edge or axis, subdividing the crease into segments (polyhinge) — open panels, petals, pop-up folds. group + group_type (primitive | edge) pick what folds; pivot_mode how the hinge line is defined; hinge_edge the edge to hinge on; hinge_angle the fold angle; divisions the crease segments; enable_inset + inset add a bevel; output_front/back/side toggle the result shells. Emits: the folded mesh; needs polygonal input.
tools.name: poly_hinge

params.desc: How the hinge line is defined.
params.name: pivot_mode

tools.description: Weld the boundaries of two polygon shells together, filling the gap with bridging polygons (polystitch) — repair seams / join separately-modeled halves. stitch_group / corners restrict which boundary polys/points are stitched; tolerance the max stitch distance; consolidate fuses coincident points; find_corners + corner_angle auto-detect corner points. Emits: the repaired mesh; needs polygonal input with matching open boundaries.
tools.name: poly_stitch

tools.description: Collapse many polygons into a single lightweight 'polysoup' primitive (polysoup) — cut memory + node overhead for dense static meshes, great before instancing / heavy scatter targets. group restricts the source; min_polys the size threshold; convex triangulates to convex polys; use_max_sides + max_sides cap polygon sides; merge_vertices welds identical verts; ignore_attribs / ignore_groups drop per-prim data. Emits: a polysoup primitive; needs polygonal input.
tools.name: poly_soup

params.desc: SOP node path to convert to a polysoup.
params.name: input

tools.description: Cut/split polygons along points, edges, or an attribute-crossing, optionally removing the cut region (polycut). group restricts affected polys; type (points | edges) the cut primitive; cut_points / cut_edges name the cut locations; strategy (remove | cut) whether to delete or just split; cut_attrib + cut_value + cut_threshold cut where an attribute crosses a value (an isocut); keep_closed re-closes the result. Emits: the cut mesh; needs polygonal input.
tools.name: poly_cut

params.desc: Delete the cut region or just split.
params.name: strategy

tools.description: Reconnect loose edges / open polylines into clean continuous paths (polypath) — tidy edge extractions and boundary curves for downstream sweep/resample. connect_ends joins nearby endpoints (within max_end_dist); connect_only_to_ends restricts joins to other endpoints (no mid-curve T-junctions); close_loops closes isolated rings. Emits: cleaned polyline curves; needs polyline / edge-curve input.
tools.name: poly_path

params.desc: SOP node path — the polylines to clean up.
params.name: input

params.desc: Join only to other endpoints (no T-junctions).
params.name: connect_only_to_ends

tools.description: Convert geometry edges into polyline curves (convertline) — extract a wireframe / edge-curves from a mesh for polywire, resample, or sweep. group restricts the source; connect_path chains edges into continuous paths; keep_order preserves group order; close_loops closes isolated rings; remove_unused drops orphaned points; compute_length + length_name write a per-primitive rest-length attribute. Emits: polyline curves; needs geometry with edges.
tools.name: convert_line

params.desc: SOP node path — the geometry whose edges to convert.
params.name: input

tools.description: Snap a ring of points/edges onto a best-fit circle (circlefromedges) — make a bolt-hole, pipe end, or wheel arch perfectly round. group + group_type pick the ring; only_boundary uses just the group boundary; explicit_radius + radius force a radius (else best-fit); scale grows/shrinks the fitted circle; output_edge_group names the result edges. Emits: the mesh with the ring circularized; needs a ring of points/edges.
tools.name: circle_from_edges

params.desc: SOP node path with the edge ring to circularize.
params.name: input

tools.description: Compute per-point orientation frames (tangent/up + rotations) along curves (orientalongcurve) — the rig for sweeping, copy-to-curve, or ribbon twist. `input` (curves) is input 0; optional `banking_curve` (input 1) drives banking. tangent_type how tangents are derived; up_vector_type + up_vector the reference up; apply_roll/roll, apply_yaw/yaw, apply_pitch/pitch add twist; scale sizes the frames; class (point | vertex); output_quaternion + quaternion_name write an `orient` quaternion for copy-to-points. Emits: the curves with orientation attributes; needs curve input.
tools.name: orient_along_curve

params.desc: SOP node path — the curves to orient (input 0).
params.name: input

tools.description: Smooth a deformed mesh while preserving surface detail (deltamush) — the standard fix for lumpy skinning / jittery deformations. `input` (deformed geometry) is input 0; optional `reference` (input 1) is the rest shape. method (uniform | edgelength); iterations + step_size the smoothing strength; pin_border holds boundary points; symmetrize + symmetry_axis mirror the smoothing; recompute_normals refreshes normals. Moves points only; needs a mesh input.
tools.name: delta_mush

params.desc: SOP node path — the deformed geometry (input 0).
params.name: input

tools.description: Evenly redistribute points across a surface to relax bunched/stretched topology (surfacerelax) — improve point distribution without changing the shape much. `input` (surface) is input 0; optional `reference` (input 1) is a reference surface the points are re-projected onto during the relax. iterations the relax passes; pin_group holds named points fixed. Moves points only; needs a surface input.
tools.name: surface_relax

params.desc: SOP node path — the surface to relax (input 0).
params.name: input

tools.description: Compute the discrete Laplace operator (cotangent / mean-value / Wachspress / Tutte weights) of a mesh and store it as a sparse matrix in attributes (laplacian) — backbone of mesh diffusion, smoothing, and geometry-processing solves. mode picks the weighting scheme; separate_mass splits out the mass matrix; diffusion + diffusion_coeff build a diffusion matrix instead; epsilon regularizes. This is an analysis/operator node (writes matrix attributes), NOT a shape deformer. Emits: the mesh + matrix attributes; needs a mesh input.
tools.name: laplacian

tools.description: Move/rotate/scale a region of points with a smooth radial falloff (softxform) — a proportional-edit / magnet grab. `group` seeds the affected region. translate / rotate / scale the transform; distance_metric how falloff distance is measured (custom | edges | global | globalconnected | surface); soft_radius the falloff reach; soft_type the profile (linear | quadratic | cubic | meta); attribs which attributes follow. Moves points only; needs geometry input.
tools.name: soft_transform

tools.description: Push points along their normals with a smooth radial falloff (softpeak) — a soft inflate/dent brush. `group` seeds the affected region. distance the push amount along normals; distance_metric how falloff distance is measured; soft_radius the falloff reach; soft_type the profile (linear | quadratic | cubic | meta); mask a global multiplier. Moves points along normals only; needs geometry input.
tools.name: soft_peak

tools.description: Deform a mesh as an elastic solid via a grab / twist / scale / pinch handle that propagates through the material (elastictransform) — feels like pulling soft rubber. `group` seeds the handle region. rigidity how stiffly the deformation spreads; mode (grab | twist | scale | pinch); grab_direction + grab_strength drive a grab; twist_angle, scale_amount, pinch_strength drive the other modes; origin the handle centre; radius the handle reach. Point-deform only; needs geometry input.
tools.name: elastic_transform

params.desc: SOP node path to elastically transform.
params.name: input

params.desc: How stiffly the deformation spreads (Poisson ratio).
params.name: rigidity

tools.description: Deform `input` points by a moving 'magnet' shape whose metaball-style field falls off with distance (magnet) — squash/stretch, dents, muscle bulges driven by a proxy shape. `input` (points to deform) is input 0; required `magnet` (the magnet-field geometry, e.g. a metaball or mesh) is input 1. translate / rotate / scale move the magnet's influence; deform_group / magnet_group restrict the regions; affect_position / affect_color / affect_normal pick what the field modulates. Without `magnet` it degrades to cooked:false. Moves points; needs 2 inputs.
tools.name: magnet

params.desc: SOP node path — the points to deform (input 0).
params.name: input

params.desc: The magnet-field geometry (input 1, required to cook).
params.name: magnet

tools.description: Push `input` points outward/inward along their normals where a 'magnet' shape overlaps them (bulge) — a fast localized swell driven by a proxy shape. `input` (points to bulge) is input 0; required `magnet` (the influence geometry) is input 1. magnitude the bulge strength (+out / -in); deform_group / magnet_group restrict the regions; normalize_weight normalizes the field weighting. Without `magnet` it degrades to cooked:false. Moves points; needs 2 inputs.
tools.name: bulge

params.desc: SOP node path — the points to bulge (input 0).
params.name: input

params.desc: The influence geometry (input 1, required to cook).
params.name: magnet

tools.description: Project `input` geometry onto a surface's UV space and crawl it across that surface (creep) — stick decals/tracks/text onto a mesh, or animate geo sliding over it. `input` (geometry to project) is input 0; required `surface` (geometry to project onto) is input 1. translate / rotate / scale slide + size the projection in the surface's parametric space; initialize (initfill | initundistort) the projection setup; set_uv + uv_name write a creep-UV attribute; path_group restricts the crawl path. Without `surface` it degrades to cooked:false. Needs 2 inputs.
tools.name: creep

params.desc: SOP node path — the geometry to project (input 0).
params.name: input

params.desc: The surface to project onto (input 1, required to cook).
params.name: surface

tools.description: Deform `input` by the difference between two matching point clouds (a rest set and a deformed set), interpolating that motion field onto the mesh (vectordeform) — cage/lattice-style deformation from arbitrary driver points. `input` (mesh to deform) is input 0; required `rest_points` (input 1) and `deformed_points` (input 2) drive the field. inner_radius / outer_radius the interpolation falloff; steps the interpolation quality; translate / rotate an extra transform. Without both driver inputs it degrades to cooked:false. Needs 3 inputs.
tools.name: vector_deform

params.desc: SOP node path — the mesh to deform (input 0).
params.name: input

params.desc: Rest driver points (input 1, required to cook).
params.name: rest_points

params.desc: New /obj chopnet name (when no chopnet given; fails on collision).
params.name: name

params.desc: Existing CHOP network to build in (else a fresh chopnet).
params.name: chopnet

tools.description: CHOP Extract Pose Drivers (extractposedrivers) — extract driver channels (joint xforms / parms) that feed a pose-space deformer. GENERATOR: builds in a fresh (or supplied `chopnet`) network. The per-driver multiparm is left at default. Data-only.
tools.name: chop_extract_pose_drivers

params.desc: New /obj chopnet name (when no chopnet given; fails on collision).
params.name: name

params.desc: Existing CHOP network to build in (else a fresh chopnet).
params.name: chopnet

tools.description: CHOP Blend Pose (blendpose) — pose-space interpolation (RBF / hyperplane) that blends example poses by driver values. OPERATOR: chained onto an `input` CHOP; input1/input2 wire aux CHOPs. Data-only (channel math).
tools.name: chop_blendpose

params.desc: Input CHOP (built in the same chopnet).
params.name: input

tools.description: CHOP Stash Pose (stashpose) — stash the current pose as a static reference pose for pose-space workflows. OPERATOR: chained onto an `input` CHOP; input1/input2 wire aux CHOPs. Data-only (channel snapshot; no file/code).
tools.name: chop_stashpose

params.desc: Input CHOP (built in the same chopnet).
params.name: input

tools.description: Pair an Input Component (input 0) with a Target Component (input 1, required) into one supervised training EXAMPLE (ml_example) — the atom of an ML dataset (features -> targets). Feed the result to ml_example_partition / ml_extract_example or the shipped export_ml_example_* writers.
tools.name: ml_example

params.desc: Treat the input side as a packed component.
params.name: use_packed_input

params.desc: Treat the target side as a packed component.
params.name: use_packed_target

params.desc: Per-point validity-mask attribute for the input.
params.name: input_validity_attrib

params.desc: Per-point validity-mask attribute for the target.
params.name: target_validity_attrib

tools.description: Pull a single training example (by index) back out of an Examples stream (ml_extractexample) — inspect/preview one sample. Input 0 = an Examples stream (e.g. from ml_example).
tools.name: ml_extract_example

params.desc: Keep the extracted component packed (else unpack to native geo).
params.name: keep_packed

tools.description: Synthesise randomised attribute values on a prototype (ml_attribgenerate) — data-augment a training set with controlled random inputs. Input 0 = the Prototype geometry. distribution is a bounded distribution-name TOKEN (uniform/gaussian/normal/poisson/...), NOT a code/expression surface.
tools.name: ml_attrib_generate

params.desc: Component count of the generated attribute.
params.name: tuple_size

params.desc: Distribution token: uniform | gaussian | normal | poisson | ...
params.name: distribution

tools.description: Sample randomised skeleton poses from a Pose Prototype (ml_posegenerate) — the training-data generator for pose-space / ML deformers. Input 0 = a KineFX skeleton (Pose Prototype). Pure generator: no model file, no training.
tools.name: ml_pose_generate

tools.description: Flatten a skeleton pose into a serial point ATTRIBUTE (ml_poseserialize) — turn a rig pose into the fixed-length feature vector an ML model consumes. Input 0 = the Pose (KineFX skeleton). NO file param (writes an attribute, not a file).
tools.name: ml_pose_serialize

params.desc: Name of the output serial attribute.
params.name: serial_attribute

params.desc: subskeleton: add the root world rotation.
params.name: include_world_rotation

params.desc: alllocal: joints whose local rotation is written.
params.name: local_rotation_group

params.desc: alllocal: joints whose local translation is written.
params.name: local_translation_group

tools.description: Split an Examples stream into parts no larger than max_part_size (ml_examplepartition) — batch a large training set into manageable chunks. Input 0 = an Examples stream.
tools.name: ml_example_partition

tools.description: WIRE-ONLY: build the learned character deformer (ml_deform) — apply a TRAINED model to deform a skin, driven by a skeleton pose. Configured but NOT cooked here (a malformed model can crash Houdini on load — same posture as onnx_inference); the USER fires the deform with a hash-pinned model. Inputs: Skin to Deform (0), Capture Pose (1), Animated Pose (2), Residual Blend Shapes (3, opt). modelfile is workdir-confined. The reload button is never pressed.
tools.name: ml_deform

params.desc: Confined trained-model path (from the model downloader allowlist).
params.name: modelfile

params.desc: Clamp the pose to the joint limits.
params.name: enforce_joint_limits
